verdict.summary: OpenWeatherMap has no OAuth. You sign up, verify your email and get an API key (appid) that you send with every request. There is no app registration, redirect URI, scope review or app review. The real limits are account-level call quotas and a required attribution to OpenWeather.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Up to 2 hours (automatic key activation after sign-up)
verdict.approval_wait: none (the key activates automatically within up to 2 hours; there is no human review)

gates.name: Free plan API key (your own account)
gates.unlocks: Your agent can call the included weather APIs (current weather, forecast, air pollution, weather maps, geocoding) with your own API key.
limits: Free plan: 60 calls/minute and 1,000,000 calls/month, no card required
One Call API: first 1,000 calls/day free, then charged per call
Requests over the limit return HTTP 429; daily limits reset between 00:00 and 00:05 UTC
Limits apply to the whole account, not to each key
No expiry for the key is stated in the docs
gates.time_to_reach: About 10 minutes of sign-up and email verification, then up to 2 hours for the key to activate automatically

gates.name: Shared use of your key (there is no test-user or install model)
gates.unlocks: Anyone using your agent can get weather data through your key. OpenWeather has no per-user authorization, test-user allowlist or install cap.
limits: All users share one account-level quota across all keys and products
Over-limit use leads to a notice asking you to upgrade or cut usage; on paid plans the key can be suspended if you don't reply
Attribution to OpenWeather is required on every tier
gates.time_to_reach: Same time as Gate 1. There is no extra step.

gates.name: Production on a self-service subscription
gates.unlocks: Higher account-level call limits for public production traffic on the Startup, Developer, Professional or Expert monthly plans, or pay-per-call One Call usage
limits: Fixed monthly calls-per-minute and calls-per-month caps for each plan
Attribution required under the ODbL licence, including for commercial use
Contracts, procurement or compliance paperwork and dedicated account management are only available through Enterprise Service
There is no app marketplace listing; the Marketplace sells data archives only
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes. Paid plans activate immediately online.

steps.title: Create an OpenWeather account
steps.detail: Sign up at home.openweathermap.org with the email address that should own the API quota and billing. The account dashboard and the API keys page require you to be signed in.

steps.title: Verify your email address
steps.detail: Click the verification link in the email OpenWeather sends you. Your personal API key (APPID) arrives in the welcome email after verification.
gotchas: If no email arrives, check your spam folder. You can resend the verification email from your account settings once at least 1 hour has passed since registration. If that also fails, contact info@openweathermap.org.

steps.title: Wait for the key to activate
steps.detail: The key activates automatically up to 2 hours after registration. Requests made before then may fail even though the key is correct.

steps.title: Create a dedicated key for your agent
steps.detail: While signed in, open the API keys page. Copy the default key or create a separate one for this agent so you can rotate it on its own later.
gotchas: Separate keys still share one account-level quota, so creating more keys does not add capacity.

steps.title: Make a test request with the key
steps.detail: Send a GET request to a Free-plan endpoint, such as current weather, with the key in the appid query parameter. Confirm the response is a success and not an auth or 429 error. OpenWeather only processes requests that include a key.

values.label: Auth parameter
values.value: appid=<your API key> (query parameter on each GET request)

steps.title: Store the key as an API-key credential, not as OAuth
steps.detail: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit, so there is no managed OAuth app and no redirect URI to configure. Store the key as a secret in your agent or in a custom API-key integration, and add it as appid on every call.
gotchas: Don't look for an OAuth client ID, secret, redirect URI or scopes. None exist.

steps.title: Add rate-limit and 429 handling
steps.detail: Your users share one account-level quota, so add caching and request throttling, and treat HTTP 429 as 'quota exceeded'. Daily limits reset between 00:00 and 00:05 UTC. A blocked account is unblocked at the next reset, not as soon as you upgrade, unless support removes the block earlier.

steps.title: Add OpenWeather attribution to your product
steps.detail: Draft and place a visible attribution to OpenWeather wherever your agent or app shows weather data. The pricing table marks attribution as Required on every tier, and the ODbL licence allows commercial use only with visible attribution.

steps.title: Pick a plan that matches expected traffic
steps.detail: Estimate monthly and per-minute call volume across all users. Compare it with the Free plan (60/min, 1M/month), One Call pay-per-call (1,000/day free) and the Startup, Developer, Professional and Expert monthly plans.

steps.title: Subscribe to a paid plan if you need one
steps.detail: Self-service subscriptions activate immediately online with no contract or compliance review. If you need contracts, procurement documents or account management, go through Enterprise Service instead.
gotchas: Going over a paid limit triggers an email asking you to move to a suitable plan. If you don't reply, the key can be suspended.

requirements.detail: You need to sign up and verify your email to receive and manage API keys.
The platform only processes requests that include the key as the appid parameter.
Usage across all keys and products counts toward one account limit. Requests over it return 429.
Required on all tiers under the ODbL licence, including commercial use.

requirements.item: Use the API, not website scraping
requirements.detail: The website terms ban scrapers, robots and spiders on the website. Get data through the API.

scopes.effect: OpenWeather has no scope or permission model. One key grants whatever your account's plan includes, so there is no scope justification or scope review.

blockers.symptom: No OAuth client, redirect URI or Composio toolkit can be found for OpenWeatherMap
blockers.cause: OpenWeather authenticates only with an API key, and Composio has no toolkit for it
blockers.fix: Use the API key as a credential, passed as appid, through a custom API-key integration or directly in your agent.

blockers.cause: Keys take up to 2 hours after registration to activate
blockers.fix: Wait up to 2 hours after registration and try again.

blockers.symptom: No verification or welcome email arrives
blockers.cause: The email was delayed or went to spam
blockers.fix: Check spam. After 1 hour, resend the email from account settings. If it still doesn't arrive, contact info@openweathermap.org.

blockers.cause: The account has gone over its daily or monthly call limit. The limit is shared across all keys.
blockers.fix: Cut or cache calls, or upgrade your plan. The block lifts at the next daily reset (00:00-00:05 UTC) unless support removes it earlier.

blockers.symptom: Key suspended after going over a paid plan's limit
blockers.cause: You didn't reply to OpenWeather's over-limit email asking you to change plans
blockers.fix: Reply to the email and move to a plan that fits your usage.

blockers.symptom: OpenWeather support won't help with problems inside your agent
blockers.cause: OpenWeather does not support use of its keys inside third-party applications
blockers.fix: Debug on your side. Use support only for account and key problems.

composio.note: Composio's catalog has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit, and OpenWeather has no OAuth. There is no managed app to start on and no OAuth app of your own to register. Use your own OpenWeather API key as a credential, through a custom API-key integration or directly in your agent, passed as the appid parameter.

evidence.claim: OpenWeather's getting-started page describes only API-key access; the key is the single credential.
evidence.quote: The API key is all you need to call any of our weather APIs.

evidence.claim: Call limits apply at the account level, not per key or product.
evidence.quote: API call limits are applied at the account level, not per API key or per product.

evidence.claim: Free-plan overuse leads to a notice asking you to upgrade or reduce calls.
evidence.quote: We will notify you and ask you to either migrate to a subscription plan that meets your needs or reduce a number of API calls accordingly.

evidence.claim: Going over a paid limit doesn't suspend the key at once; it is suspended if you don't reply to the email.
evidence.quote: we won't immediately suspend your API key if you exceed the call limit.

evidence.claim: Daily limits reset between 00:00 and 00:05 UTC, and blocked accounts unblock at the next reset.
evidence.quote: Daily API call limits are reset every day between 00:00 and 00:05 UTC.

evidence.claim: HTTP 429 is returned only when calls go over the daily or monthly limit.
evidence.quote: You can receive a "429" error in only one case

evidence.claim: Attribution is marked Required on every tier, including Free.
evidence.quote: Attribution

evidence.claim: API access is under the ODbL licence, which allows commercial use with visible attribution.
evidence.quote: API access under the ODbL licence

evidence.claim: Self-service subscriptions activate immediately with no contract or compliance review; those services are for Enterprise only.
evidence.quote: Immediate online activation

evidence.claim: OpenWeather does not support use of its API keys inside third-party applications.
evidence.quote: we do not provide technical support for using an OpenWeather API key inside third-party applications

evidence.claim: The Marketplace sells historical data archives, not third-party apps.
evidence.quote: Purchase reliable historical weather data archives in the Weather Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Every request must carry the account's API key.
evidence.quote: Our platform only processes the API requests with an API key included.

evidence.claim: The API keys page requires you to be signed in.
evidence.quote: You need to sign in or sign up before continuing.

evidence.claim: The website terms ban automated scraping of the website, which is separate from the API.
evidence.quote: page-scraper

evidence.claim: A third-party catalog lists OpenWeather's auth method as API key only.
evidence.quote: Auth methods: set to

evidence.claim: No OAuth scopes exist for OpenWeather APIs, so there is no scope review.
No app review, listing, domain verification, security assessment or minimum-install rule was found.
No install caps apply; the only limits are per-account call limits.
The key is passed as an appid query parameter on each GET request, and no scope model is described.
evidence.quote: add your API key as an *appid* parameter to the GET request

evidence.claim: Self-service sign-up and email verification deliver the key, which is listed on the API keys page where more keys can be created.
evidence.quote: you will receive your personal API key (APPID)

evidence.claim: A new API key activates automatically within up to two hours of registration.
evidence.quote: Your API key will be activated automatically, up to 2 hours after your successful registration.

evidence.claim: The verification email can be resent after 1 hour; otherwise check spam and contact info@openweathermap.org.
evidence.quote: Wait at least 1 hour after registration. You can then resend the verification email from your account settings

evidence.claim: The Free plan allows 60 calls/minute and 1,000,000 calls/month with no card required.
evidence.quote: 60 API calls/minute, 1,000,000 calls/month

evidence.claim: One Call API is pay-per-call, with the first 1,000 calls per day free.
evidence.quote: First 1,000 API calls per day are FREE

evidence.claim: Paid self-service plans are fixed monthly subscriptions with account-level caps.
evidence.quote: Price per month

open_questions: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit. It is unconfirmed whether a custom API-key integration in Composio can inject appid as a query parameter.
No key expiry or rotation policy is documented. The key appears to be long-lived.
The exact One Call per-call overage rate and the limits for each paid plan should be checked on the pricing page before you commit. The Enterprise terms and the Terms of sale PDF were not reviewed.
No OpenWeather changelog from 2025-2026 was found, so recent policy changes could not be checked.
